checks.observation: All eight have maximum link-point degree5, including both shared-leaf Q8 cases. After at most3 deletions, at least13 triples remain, whereas two support points meet at most10. Every ambient four-cover therefore has at least3 support points. Each support cover triple permits at most2 actual completions by global triple codegree, and each pure support four-set occurs at most once by simplicity. The bound 2|C3|+|P4| is a valid union upper bound even with arbitrary exterior points or multiple covering triples in one member. The code distributes each support subset to every deletion superset of its missed-triple set, matching the complete relation.
checks.scope: Arbitrary-exterior cover transfer and eight-model domain

checks.method: Rebuilt each recorded exceptional link and deletion set using fresh literal-set code; directly enumerated its support three- and four-covers, without calling the saved producer or replayer. Also checked every eleven-element subset of its twelve cover candidates.
checks.observation: Each exception has zero three-covers, exactly12 four-covers, one common point and union size7, agreeing with the receipt. Thus no exterior cover is omitted. Removing the common point gives triples on six points with pair codegree at most2, implying 3m<=2*15 and m<=10. Every eleven-candidate selection also directly violates a lifted pair cap. The exceptions are two each in models 0/0, 0/1 and 0/2; no generic sunflower-free status of the twelve candidates was assumed.

checks.method: Read the exact down-set derivation and the completed-vector block in d16_fibre_reconstruction.cpp; compared occupied-coordinate masks with explicitly labelled actual cone sets in a nonunit-weight example.
checks.observation: D_i is the union of all star members in adjacent occupied fibres. Because those fibre blocks are disjoint and nonempty, D_j subset D_i is exactly occupied-mask inclusion. The code uses missing[i]=adj[i]&occupied and tests missing[j]&~missing[i]==0; q[i] is independently recomputed as the sum of t[j], and the left side sums a[j]-t[j]. The example with q6<=q3 but nonnested actual sets is correctly rejected by mask inclusion. No weight is collapsed to one member.
checks.scope: Actual deletion sets versus cardinalities and multiplicities

checks.method: Checked the graph-to-cover implication in D16-complete-argument.md and D16-fibre-independent-preparation.md; inspected the C++ first-occupied-edge partition, conditional ceilings and final domain checks.
checks.observation: Only image nonedges are used to force intersection. A star member has at most b_i-q_i possible graph neighbours, so minimum degree24 yields q_i<=r_i on occupied star fibres without requiring all permitted edges. Nonstar members counted by the down-set inequality meet every undeleted cone for the same reason. The first-edge partition retains every nonindependent support under its unique seed; ceilings impose only already-occupied neighbour budgets and exclusion of earlier edges. Final vectors recheck total16, full q masses and all applicable cover inequalities. This was source and bridge inspection, not a fresh full 124,323-vector replay.

findings.disposition: The actual C++ implementation compares occupied-neighbour masks and separately sums full masses, so it avoids this failure. This is an interface test, not a claimed complete feasible star vector.
findings.statement: Comparing deletion cardinalities alone would be unsound: for A3 and t=(2,1,0,0,1,0,0,0), q6=1<=q3=2 but D6 is not a subset of D3.

content.summary: The inspected degree16 cover and fibre interfaces retain arbitrary exterior completions, correct multiplicities and actual deletion-set inclusion. All six raw12 exceptions were reconstructed directly and justify the bound10. No hidden complete-blowup premise or lost-multiplicity defect was found. Frozen hashes and roster identity match; earlier resolved revisions remain intact.
